messages:
anya: Heads-up — I saw a perf regression on nightly for FlashPaged (SM90, Triton-built). p99 jumped ~30% on long-seq workloads after the kernel selector change. Anyone else seeing this?
dan: saw that in dashboards too. rough numbers? which commit landed the selector tweak?
anya: regression started around 1830930000 commit (kernel-selector: prefer-triton-for-flashvariants). 2x worse on some sequences when KV hit rate low. p50 mostly fine, p99 worst.
mohit: can you paste the benchmark command you used? I want to reproduce locally on our SM90 test rig.
anya: repro script: ```bash
./bench_runner --model=gpt-7b --seq_len=4096 --batch=1 --kv_paged=true --kernel_policy=selector_v2 --warmup=20 --iters=200
```
benchbot: perf snapshot (1831001150): throughput=210 tok/s, p50=12ms/token, p95=48ms/token, p99=86ms/token (SM90 Triton FlashPaged).
samir: interesting — on SM80 with CUDA kernels the same script yields throughput=260 tok/s and p99=65ms/token. meaning selector_v2 picked Triton flash variant on SM90 but it regresses vs the CUDA fallback.
dan: did we change any shared memory or threadblock sizing heuristics in selector_v2? small differences in kernel launch params can blow up tail latency.
mohit: I benchmarked the Triton-built flash kernel with nvprof/Nsight. NVTX shows heavy stalls in the attention compute stage for page-fault-like patterns when KV cache misses are frequent. Could be memory layout / coalescing mismatch on SM90.
anya: attaching minimal perf logs: ```
[run 1] top breakdown:
  memcpy H2D: 3.2%
  kv_loads (device): 21.4%
  attention_kernel_triton: 58.9% (stalls: 37%)
  postprocess: 4.5%
```
mohit: if stalls are high, perhaps Triton kernels are not picking the best vectorized loads on SM90. We should try building Triton with `--triton-min-arch=sm_90` and also compare with CUDA handwritten kernels compiled with nvcc targeting sm_90.
sanir: (typo: samir) I mean we should test fused attention too. Fused Flash2 on SM90 earlier had better L2 utilization; maybe the selector needs a utilization model per-arch.
dan: proposed quick plan: 1) run microbench matrix across [SM80, SM90] x [Triton-flash, CUDA-flash, fused-attn] for seq=256/1024/4096; 2) capture NVTX + kernel occupancy + L2 hit rates; 3) add heuristic to selector to prefer CUDA-flash for KV-miss-heavy profiles on SM90 until we root cause.
anya: I'm on step 1 now. Initial run shows CUDA-flash has ~10-18% lower p99 on 4096 when kv_miss_rate>0.3.
mohit: good. also try toggling `prefetch_kv` in paged backend — maybe Triton kernel expects different prefetch pattern.
anya: tried prefetch_kv=true -> p99 improved a bit but not fully. So it's not just prefetch.
infra-bot: deploy note: test-rig-sm90 queued for extended profiling, ETA ~25m.
samir: another datapoint: batching behavior interacts — when max_batch_tokens is high we see better amortization on CUDA kernels; Triton variant seems more sensitive to batch size, likely because of less flexible kernel tiling. We should add a tiny batching heuristic in the selector that penalizes Triton for batch-token variance.
dan: can we add a cheap estimator: expected_token_amort = avg_seq_len * expected_batch_size; if < threshold prefer CUDA kernel? That's quick and reversible.
mohit: yes, implement as a fallback rule in selector_v2. I'll open a PR with a flag `kernel_selector.heuristics.batch_amort_threshold` default 4096 tokens.
anya: SG. Also filing an issue to dig into Triton codegen differences on SM90 (memory coalescing + ld matrices). I'll attach NVTX traces once infra finishes. :eyes:
benchbot: quick summary added to the perf board: https://board.internal/redwood/perf/issue/512
anya: thanks — will follow up with traces and a proposed selector patch after reproductions. :thumbsup:
